items.title: PHP Warns of Critical Security Flaws Affecting All Supported Versions, Fixes Coming November 19
items.summary: The maintainers of the PHP programming language on Wednesday issued an advisory announcing an upcoming security release that addresses critical flaws. The release is scheduled for November 19, 2026, between 2 and 2:30 p.m. UTC. "These releases are part of PHP's regular four-week release cycle and will address security vulnerabilities affecting all supported PHP versions," the maintainers said.

items.title: Who Runs the Ransomware Group Qilin?
items.summary: The cybercrime group Qilin has emerged as the world's most active ransomware affiliate program, claiming at least 365 victim organizations in the past three months alone. But even top Russian hackers make operational security mistakes, and the administrator of Qilin has made a few key missteps over the last decade that all point to a 36-year-old man living in St. Petersburg, Russia.

Details. Slashdot thread.

items.title: Constant-Round Secure Distributed Decoding and HQC Threshold Decryption
items.summary: Threshold public-key encryption schemes enable decryption only with the participation of enough partial secret key holders. In this article, we propose the first dedicated protocol for distributed decryption of HQC ciphertexts. items.title: G+G: A Fiat-Shamir Lattice Signature Based on Convolved Gaussians
items.summary: We describe an adaptation of Schnorr's signature to the lattice setting, which relies on Gaussian convolution rather than flooding or rejection sampling as previous approaches. It does not involve any abort, can be proved secure in the ROM and QROM using existing analyses of the Fiat-Shamir transform, and enjoys smaller signature sizes (both asymptotically and for concrete security levels).
